A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FictionalQA dataset, generation pipeline, and memorization experiments. The text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the title and formatting changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama and Gemma finetuning experiments measuring verbatim memorization, document loss, question-conditioned answer loss, and MCQ accuracy, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds sample-level error analysis and entity/word-overlap results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Appendix D.6.1 adds an alternative MCQ construction procedure using GPT-5-mini to generate distractors from each question's supporting fictsheet and document. This supplements the existing answer-pool ranking procedure; the original pipeline and methods underlying the reported experiments remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same fictional events and document styles, Dolma webtext, and TriviaQA. The new analyses and alternative distractors reuse existing fictional content without adding an evaluated domain, population, or task.

E2.justification: The Llama/Gemma comparisons and Base Webtext controls are unchanged, including the appendix experiments. GPT-5-mini generates the alternative MCQs; it is not an added benchmark comparator, and those MCQs are not used in the reported evaluation experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds diagnostic protocols grouping questions by initial/final correctness, calculating conditional error rates, and comparing entity/word Jaccard overlap. The original finetuning settings, splits, model sizes, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B substantially investigates Figure 8's held-out-event improvement through an answer-deduplication check, concrete MCQ case studies, correctness-transition analysis, distractor-error analysis, and distributional-overlap comparisons. V1 discussed possible MCQ artifacts but did not provide these diagnostic investigations.

E5.justification: For the alternative MCQs, Appendix D.6.1 newly specifies four blind and four informed answering attempts per question, with averaged grade annotations. This is additional repeated-annotation reporting, not evidence of increased training repetitions; no training-run uncertainty estimates are added.

E6.justification: The existing plotted results are unchanged, but Appendix B adds substantial diagnostic findings. Table 2 reports that 26.42% of initially incorrect training questions and 25.03% of validation questions become correct; Tables 3–5 add entity/word-overlap measurements across correctness groups. Table 1 restates Figure 8's endpoints rather than demonstrating a new performance gain.

T1.justification: The working definitions of sequence, factual, and stylistic memorization remain unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs. The added Jaccard comparisons are empirical diagnostics, not new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: V2 removes the introduction's categorical claim that no prior work studied factual-knowledge acquisition dynamics under realistic LLM training settings. The abstract also changes from 'teasing apart' memorization forms to studying them, while retaining the dataset contribution and four principal findings.

C2.justification: Appendix B substantially expands interpretation of the central MCQ ambiguity. It argues that similar training/validation error transitions favor distributional learning and that simple entity/word overlap does not explain which validation questions improve. It explicitly acknowledges that an additional atomic-learning contribution is not conclusively established and that manual inspection is incomplete.

D1.justification: V2 documents the alternative MCQ split, its grade fields, and gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 with low reasoning effort and verbosity. Dataset, training-split, and reformatted-TriviaQA access references change from tomg-group-umd to jwkirchenbauer. Existing finetuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds McCoy et al. (2019) to contextualize being 'right for the wrong reasons,' specifies New News's 75 articles and 375 questions, and removes the categorical no-prior-work assertion. The extended related-work survey otherwise remains substantively unchanged, moving from Appendix B to C.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, updates an author name, folds Dataset Release into Section 3.1, introduces numbered experimental subsections, and moves detailed annotation discussion into the appendix. These are limited organizational and prose refinements; most existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds five diagnostic tables and boxed question/ranking examples, substantially expanding visual reporting of the MCQ analysis. It also changes title and heading typography, page flow, figure sizing, and several captions. The original eleven figures retain their underlying contents.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through concrete investigation of MCQ artifacts, detailed error/overlap results, and documentation of an alternative construction procedure. These gains are limited: the reported experiments still use the original artifact-prone MCQs, and the added analyses do not conclusively separate factual from distributional learning or establish that the alternative resolves the problem.
